title: Graph Nodev0.1.0
description: A node in a linked graph. Nodes represent domain entities (buildings, roads, sensors, etc.) identified by a UUID and classified by a type string. The node's UUID identity is its key in the enclosing `nodes` dictionary — the object itself carries no `id` field. Geometric representations are attached via the optional `representations` dict — each entry groups a set of geometry UUIDs from the graph's `geometries` dict with a CRS reference (by UUID) and an optional outer pose. Arbitrary application-specific properties are carried in the optional `metadata` object.

type.description: String classifying this node. May be a plain application-defined string (e.g. "Building", "Road", "Sensor") or a contexted compact IRI (e.g. "bot:Building") whose prefix is declared in the document `context`. The schema enforces only that the value is a non-empty string; term validity for a contexted type is governed by the namespace's `vocabulary` (ontology), not by JSON Schema. A node carries a single type; multiple JSON-LD-style types are expressed as a metadata entry with a list value (e.g. an `rdf:type` key).

representations.description: Optional UUID-keyed dictionary of geometric representations of this node. Each entry is purely a geometry-to-CRS binding: it groups one or more geometry UUIDs (referencing keys in the enclosing graph's `geometries` dict) with a CRS reference (by UUID) and an optional outer pose. Representations carry no metadata — descriptive metadata about the encoding (LOD, provenance) lives on the node's `metadata`. A node typically has one representation; multiple entries are for the same geometry in alternative serializations (e.g. an OBJ and a PLY GeometryLink, distinguished by their `mime`) or different CRS projections. Distinct encodings that need their own identity or relations (e.g. a conversion recorded via `prov:wasDerivedFrom`) are modelled as separate nodes.

crsId.description: UUID referencing a CRS entry in the enclosing graph's `crs` dictionary. The CRS defines the coordinate reference system that real-world coordinates land in after all geometry innerposes and the optional outerpose are applied. Referential integrity — that this UUID exists in `crs` — cannot be enforced by JSON Schema and MUST be verified at the application layer.

outerpose.description: Optional affine transform applied on top of each referenced geometry's own innerpose. Useful when multiple geometries are positioned as a unit at a specific site. If absent, each geometry's innerpose delivers coordinates directly into the CRS.

geometryIds.description: Non-empty array of unique UUID strings, each referencing a key in the enclosing graph's `geometries` dict. A representation may reference multiple geometry primitives (e.g. separate wall and roof polygons composing one building shell). Referential integrity — that each UUID exists in `geometries` — cannot be enforced by JSON Schema and MUST be verified at the application layer.

metadata.description: Optional key-value map of node properties. This is the home for all descriptive metadata about the node, including identity/application attributes, level-of-detail (`lod:gis`), and provenance (`provenance:*`) — representations carry none. Each value is a value object ({value, type?, language?, direction?, unit?}) — see objects.schema.json#/$defs/value. Keys may be contexted compact IRIs whose prefix is declared in the document `context`.
